question: Should reaction-triggered turns use one shared cross-channel notification-wake policy, land as channel-specific opt-in settings first, or remain passive system events for now?
rationale: The issue asks for new public wake/config semantics across multiple channels, and current open PRs demonstrate competing scope choices that automation should not pick unilaterally.

options.title: Shared opt-in wake policy
options.body: Define one queue/wake/off-style contract and apply it consistently after existing reaction notification and access filters; this best matches the cross-channel request and avoids drift.

options.title: Channel-specific first
options.body: Land a focused Discord or Telegram path first and keep this broader issue open until the remaining channels and naming are settled.

options.title: Defer core wake semantics
options.body: Keep reactions as passive system events and route richer behavior to hooks/plugins until maintainers are ready to own a core config surface.

recommendation.title: Shared opt-in wake policy
recommendation.body: Define one queue/wake/off-style contract and apply it consistently after existing reaction notification and access filters; this best matches the cross-channel request and avoids drift.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the open shared policy PR and has recent history on both heartbeat/runtime and channel system-event surfaces.
